papers.title: Lassa fever outbreak across two tertiary hospitals in Rivers State, Nigeria: clinical spectrum, healthcare-associated infection, contact investigation and public health response
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Lassa fever (LF) remains a major public health threat in Nigeria, with outcomes influenced by timely diagnosis and treatment and by potential healthcare-associated transmission. We characterised confirmed LF cases and conducted contact investigations at two tertiary hospitals in Rivers State, Nigeria, during the 2024 outbreak. Methods We conducted a descriptive two-centre case series of confirmed LF cases identified at the University of Port Harcourt Teaching Hospital (UPTH) and Rivers State University Teaching Hospital (RSUTH) from January 23 to August 13, 2024. Cases were confirmed by real-time reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) for Lassa virus. Clinical, epidemiological, laboratory, treatment, and outcome data were obtained from hospital and public health records. Contact investigations included risk stratification, 21-day active surveillance, clinical assessment and RT-PCR testing of symptomatic contacts, and ribavirin post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) for eligible high-risk contacts. Analysis was descriptive. Results Seven laboratory-confirmed cases were identified: five community-associated and two healthcare-associated infections among high-risk healthcare-worker contacts of the UPTH index case. Patients were aged 21–61 years, and four were male. Five patients had gastrointestinal and haemorrhagic manifestations (71.43%), while three had AKI and neurological manifestations (42.86%). Five patients survived, and two died, giving a case fatality proportion of 28.57%. Both deaths occurred in community-associated index cases before therapeutic ribavirin could be administered. Contact surveillance detected the two healthcare-associated infections, which had mild clinical courses. At UPTH, 106 primary contacts were identified; 42 were high-risk, of whom 31 developed acute febrile illness, and two were confirmed with secondary LF. All 42 high-risk contacts received ribavirin PEP. At RSUTH, eight high-risk contacts were monitored; one received PEP, and none developed secondary infection. One survivor with severe renal disease required six haemodialysis sessions and was discharged after 18 days. Conclusions The LF outbreak demonstrated substantial clinical heterogeneity, ranging from mild healthcare-associated infection to severe multisystem disease and death. Contact investigation and prospective surveillance enabled detection of healthcare-associated secondary infections and facilitated targeted PEP. Strengthening early recognition, healthcare-worker protection, laboratory confirmation, contact surveillance, and timely treatment should remain priorities for LF preparedness and outbreak response in Nigeria.

At UPTH, 106 primary contacts were identified; 42 were high-risk, of whom 31 developed acute febrile illness, and two were confirmed with secondary LF. All 42 high-risk contacts received ribavirin PEP. At RSUTH, eight high-risk contacts were monitored; one received PEP, and none developed secondary infection. One survivor with severe renal disease required six haemodialysis sessions and was discharged after 18 days. Conclusions The LF outbreak demonstrated substantial clinical heterogeneity, ranging from mild healthcare-associated infection to severe multisystem disease and death. Contact investigation and prospective surveillance enabled detection of healthcare-associated secondary infections and facilitated targeted PEP. Strengthening early recognition, healthcare-worker protection, laboratory confirmation, contact surveillance, and timely treatment should remain priorities for LF preparedness and outbreak response in Nigeria.

papers.title_zh: 尼日利亚河流州两家三级医院的 拉沙热 暴发:临床谱、医疗保健相关感染、接触者调查和公共卫生应对
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Lassa fever (LF) remains a major public health threat in Nigeria, with outcomes influenced by timely diagnosis and treatment and by potential healthcare-associated transmission. We characterised confirmed LF cases and conducted contact investigations at two tertiary hospitals in Rivers State, Nigeria, during the 2024 outbreak. Methods We conducted a descriptive two-centre case series of confirmed LF cases identified at the University of Port Harcourt Teaching Hospital (UPTH) and Rivers State University Teaching Hospital (RSUTH) from January 23 to August 13, 2024. Cases were confirmed by real-time reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) for Lassa virus. Clinical, epidemiological, laboratory, treatment, and outcome data were obtained from hospital and public health records. Contact investigations included risk stratification, 21-day active surveillance, clinical assessment and RT-PCR testing of symptomatic contacts, and ribavirin post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) for eligible high-risk contacts. Analysis was descriptive. Results Seven laboratory-confirmed cases were identified: five community-associated and two healthcare-associated infections among high-risk healthcare-worker contacts of the UPTH index case. Patients were aged 21–61 years, and four were male. Five patients had gastrointestinal and haemorrhagic manifestations (71.43%), while three had AKI and neurological manifestations (42.86%). Five patients survived, and two died, giving a case fatality proportion of 28.57%. Both deaths occurred in community-associated index cases before therapeutic ribavirin could be administered. Contact surveillance detected the two healthcare-associated infections, which had mild clinical courses. At UPTH, 106 primary contacts were identified; 42 were high-risk, of whom 31 developed acute febrile illness, and two were confirmed with secondary LF. All 42 high-risk contacts received ribavirin PEP. At RSUTH, eight high-risk contacts were monitored; one received PEP, and none developed secondary infection. One survivor with severe renal disease required six haemodialysis sessions and was discharged after 18 days. Conclusions The LF outbreak demonstrated substantial clinical heterogeneity, ranging from mild healthcare-associated infection to severe multisystem disease and death. Contact investigation and prospective surveillance enabled detection of healthcare-associated secondary infections and facilitated targeted PEP. Strengthening early recognition, healthcare-worker protection, laboratory confirmation, contact surveillance, and timely treatment should remain priorities for LF preparedness and outbreak response in Nigeria.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要背景 拉沙热 (LF) 仍然是尼日利亚的主要公共卫生威胁,其结果受到及时的 诊断 和 治疗 以及潜在的医疗保健相关的 传播 的影响。我们在 2024 年 暴发 期间对尼日利亚河流州的两家三级医院进行了确诊的 LF 病例的特征分析和接触者调查。方法 我们对 2024 年 1 月 23 日至 8 月 13 日在哈科特港大学教学医院 (UPTH) 和河流州立大学教学医院 (RSUTH) 发现的 LF 确诊病例进行了描述性的两中心病例系列研究。病例通过拉沙病毒实时逆转录聚合酶链反应 (RT-PCR) 进行确诊。临床、流行病学、实验室、治疗 和结果数据从医院和公共卫生记录中获得。接触者调查包括风险分层、21 天主动 监测、有症状接触者的临床评估和 RT-PCR 检测,以及对符合条件的高风险接触者进行利巴韦林暴露后预防 (PEP)。分析是描述性的。结果 确定了 7 例实验室确诊病例:在 UPTH 指标病例的高危医护人员接触者中,有 5 例是社区相关感染,2 例是医疗保健相关感染。患者年龄为 21-61 岁,其中 4 名是男性。5 例患者出现胃肠道和出血表现(71.43%),3 例患者出现 AKI 和神经系统表现(42.86%)。存活5例,死亡2例,病死率为28.57%。这两例死亡均发生在使用利巴韦林治疗之前的社区相关指示病例中。联系人 监测 检测到两种与医疗保健相关的感染,其临床病程较轻。在 UPTH,确定了 106 名主要联系人;42 人为高危人群,其中 31 人出现急性发热性疾病,2 人确诊为继发性 LF。所有 42 名高危接触者均接受了利巴韦林 PEP。在 RSUTH,八名高风险接触者受到监控;一名患者接受了 PEP,没有人出现继发感染。一名患有严重肾病的幸存者需要进行六次血液透析,并在 18 天后出院。结论 LF 暴发 表现出显着的临床异质性,从轻微的医疗保健相关感染到严重的多系统疾病和死亡。接触者调查和前瞻性 监测 能够检测与医疗保健相关的继发感染,并促进有针对性的 PEP。加强早期识别、医护人员保护、实验室确认、联系 监测 和及时 治疗 应仍然是尼日利亚 LF 准备和 暴发 响应的优先事项。

papers.title: Retaining Participants in a Prospective Epidemiological Study Involving Blood Draws Through Sustained Engagement: Lessons from Enable 1.0 Incidence Study on Lassa Fever Infection in Abakaliki, Southeast Nigeria
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Participant retention is critical in longitudinal studies involving blood draws. Enable 1.0 Incidence Study on Lassa Fever was conducted to estimate Lassa virus infection and disease to inform outbreak preparedness and vaccine research. This nested analysis aimed to explore community engagement strategies employed to retain participants. Methods Enable 1.0 was a multi-site, multi-country, prospective cohort study (December 2020–December 2023) aiming to estimate the incidence of Lassa virus infection and symptomatic Lassa fever disease. In Abakaliki Nigeria, the study tracked Lassa virus seroconversion among 1,000 healthy participants across 10 communities in three Local Government Areas. Community Liaison Officers, village guides, and field workers sustained engagement through fortnightly visits and sensitization meetings. Fieldworkers completed a semi-structured Google Forms questionnaire documenting their experiences and observations across 713 participants, including participant reception, retention threats, and their engagement strategies. The data were analyzed descriptively using IBM-SPSS Statistics Version-25. Results Overall, the study achieved a 90.5% participant retention rate over the 24-month follow-up period across the full cohort of 1,000 participants. Based on fieldworker reports covering 713 participants, 91.4% (652/713) completed the study, while 8.6% (61/713) did not. Reported retention threats (102/713; 14.3%) included inadequate compensation (52/713; 7.3%), family pressure (48/713; 6.7%), and fear of blood rituals (37/713; 5.2%). Reasons for non-completion were relocation (23/713; 3.2%), refusal (15/713; 2.1%), family opposition (6/713; 0.8%), and death (6/713; 0.8%). Key retention strategies included engaging village guides (439/713; 61.6%), incentives (293/713; 41.1%), family support (152/713; 21.3%), and involvement of traditional leaders (151/713; 21.2%). Despite rumours related to blood rituals, sustained community engagement and unscheduled home visits supported by reassurance from the study technical team helped dispel misinformation, with 88.2% (629/713) of participants remaining warmly receptive to fieldworkers throughout the study. Conclusion The Enable 1.0 study demonstrated that high participant retention is achievable in resource-limited high-risk settings when structured community engagement and rapid response mechanisms are integrated into study implementation. Future studies should embed engagement structures, institutionalize rapid responses to rumours, and prioritize transparent communication to strengthen retention and public trust.

Enable 1.0 Incidence Study on Lassa Fever was conducted to estimate Lassa virus infection and disease to inform outbreak preparedness and vaccine research. This nested analysis aimed to explore community engagement strategies employed to retain participants. Methods Enable 1.0 was a multi-site, multi-country, prospective cohort study (December 2020–December 2023) aiming to estimate the incidence of Lassa virus infection and symptomatic Lassa fever disease. In Abakaliki Nigeria, the study tracked Lassa virus seroconversion among 1,000 healthy participants across 10 communities in three Local Government Areas. Community Liaison Officers, village guides, and field workers sustained engagement through fortnightly visits and sensitization meetings. Fieldworkers completed a semi-structured Google Forms questionnaire documenting their experiences and observations across 713 participants, including participant reception, retention threats, and their engagement strategies. The data were analyzed descriptively using IBM-SPSS Statistics Version-25. Results Overall, the study achieved a 90.5% participant retention rate over the 24-month follow-up period across the full cohort of 1,000 participants. Based on fieldworker reports covering 713 participants, 91.4% (652/713) completed the study, while 8.6% (61/713) did not. Reported retention threats (102/713; 14.3%) included inadequate compensation (52/713; 7.3%), family pressure (48/713; 6.7%), and fear of blood rituals (37/713; 5.2%). Reasons for non-completion were relocation (23/713; 3.2%), refusal (15/713; 2.1%), family opposition (6/713; 0.8%), and death (6/713; 0.8%). Key retention strategies included engaging village guides (439/713; 61.6%), incentives (293/713; 41.1%), family support (152/713; 21.3%), and involvement of traditional leaders (151/713; 21.2%). Despite rumours related to blood rituals, sustained community engagement and unscheduled home visits supported by reassurance from the study technical team helped dispel misinformation, with 88.2% (629/713) of participants remaining warmly receptive to fieldworkers throughout the study. Conclusion The Enable 1.0 study demonstrated that high participant retention is achievable in resource-limited high-risk settings when structured community engagement and rapid response mechanisms are integrated into study implementation. Future studies should embed engagement structures, institutionalize rapid responses to rumours, and prioritize transparent communication to strengthen retention and public trust.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 在涉及抽血的纵向研究中,参与者的保留至关重要。启用 1.0 发病率 对 拉沙热 进行研究是为了估计拉沙病毒感染和疾病,为 暴发 准备工作和 疫苗 研究提供信息。这种嵌套分析旨在探索用于留住参与者的社区参与策略。方法 Enable 1.0 是一项多中心、多国家、前瞻性 队列研究 研究(2020 年 12 月至 2023 年 12 月),旨在估计拉沙病毒感染和有症状的 拉沙热 疾病的 发病率。在尼日利亚阿巴卡利基,该研究追踪了三个地方政府区域 10 个社区 1,000 名健康参与者的拉沙病毒血清转化情况。社区联络官、村庄向导和现场工作人员通过每两周一次的访问和宣传会议持续参与。现场工作人员完成了一份半结构化的 Google 表单调查问卷,记录了他们对 713 名参与者的经验和观察,包括参与者的接受情况、保留威胁以及他们的参与策略。使用 IBM-SPSS Statistics Version-25 对数据进行描述性分析。结果 总体而言,在 24 个月的随访期内,该研究在整个 队列研究 的 1,000 名参与者中实现了 90.5% 的参与者保留率。根据涵盖 713 名参与者的现场工作人员报告,91.4% (652/713) 完成了研究,而 8.6% (61/713) 没有完成。报告的保留威胁(102/713;14.3%)包括薪酬不足(52/713;7.3%)、家庭压力(48/713;6.7%)和对血腥仪式的恐惧(37/713;5.2%)。未完成的原因包括搬迁(23/713;3.2%)、拒绝(15/713;2.1%)、家人反对(6/713;0.8%)和死亡(6/713;0.8%)。关键的保留策略包括聘请乡村向导(439/713;61.6%)、激励措施(293/713;41.1%)、家庭支持(152/713;21.3%)以及传统领导人的参与(151/713;21.2%)。尽管存在与血仪式有关的谣言,但在研究技术团队的保证支持下,持续的社区参与和不定期的家访有助于消除错误信息,88.2% (629/713) 的参与者在整个研究过程中仍然热情地接受现场工作人员。结论 Enable 1.0 研究表明,当将结构化社区参与和快速响应机制纳入研究实施时,在资源有限的高风险环境中可以实现较高的参与者保留率。未来的研究应该嵌入参与结构,将谣言的快速反应制度化,并优先考虑透明的沟通,以加强保留和公众信任。

papers.title: Mortality-based reporting completeness index for Lassa fever surveillance in Nigeria, 2012-2025.
papers.abstract: Lassa fever is endemic across West Africa, yet the completeness of national surveillance remains poorly quantified. We developed and applied a Reporting Completeness Index (RCI) to quantify surveillance performance in Nigeria from 2012 to 2025. Annual confirmed cases and deaths reported by the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention were analysed. RCI was defined as the ratio of reported confirmed cases to expected cases estimated from reported deaths using a reference case fatality rate of 16.5%. Uncertainty was assessed using Monte Carlo simulation, while Mann-Kendall and Spearman tests, Sen's slope, change-point detection, and sensitivity analyses across five CFR assumptions (10-25%) assessed temporal patterns and robustness. National RCI increased from 26.1% in 2012 to a mean of 103.6% after 2019, representing an approximately four-fold improvement. The upward trend was significant (Mann-Kendall τ = 0.51, p = 0.015; Sen's slope = 5.84% per year), with a structural break identified in 2019 (p < 0.001). The improvement coincided with expanded laboratory capacity and deployment of SORMAS. RCI provides a transparent, reproducible approach for monitoring surveillance completeness in resource-limited settings.

papers.title: Lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus: an overview of a neglected neurotropic zoonosis
papers.abstract: Lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV), a rodent-borne mammarenavirus, is endemic worldwide and under-appreciated although it has neurotropism and potential for serious clinical disease. LCMV is commonly carried by the house mouse ( Mus musculus ), thus being distributed globally in urban and rural areas. Transmission occurs primarily through inhalation of aerosolised excreta from infected rodents or contaminated secretions, with additional routes including solid organ transplantation, rarely, and vertical transmission. In humans, LCMV infection may vary from an inapparent or self-limiting febrile disease to more severe diseases such as aseptic meningitis or meningoencephalitis especially in immunocompromised patients. Congenital infections have been reported to cause chorioretinitis, intracranial calcifications, a variety of neurologic malformations, intellectual disability, neurodevelopmental problems, and death of the foetus. To date, 88 congenital cases of LCMV infection have been documented in the literature, and 5 donor-derived transplant-associated clusters involving 17 recipients have been reported worldwide. The objective of this narrative review is to provide a comprehensive and up-to-date overview of LCMV. Specifically, the review summarizes current knowledge on its virological characteristics, epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention. Particular attention is given to congenital infection, transplant-associated disease, and the evolving epidemiology of LCMV, with emphasis on its public health relevance within a One Health framework. Laboratory approaches and diagnostic challenges are also discussed, including relevant biosafety considerations. Finally, the review highlights persisting knowledge gaps and identifies priority areas for future research, surveillance, and public health action.
papers.journal: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

source_records.abstract: Lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV), a rodent-borne mammarenavirus, is endemic worldwide and under-appreciated although it has neurotropism and potential for serious clinical disease. LCMV is commonly carried by the house mouse ( Mus musculus ), thus being distributed globally in urban and rural areas. Particular attention is given to congenital infection, transplant-associated disease, and the evolving epidemiology of LCMV, with emphasis on its public health relevance within a One Health framework. Laboratory approaches and diagnostic challenges are also discussed, including relevant biosafety considerations. Finally, the review highlights persisting knowledge gaps and identifies priority areas for future research, surveillance, and public health action.

papers.abstract_zh: 淋巴细胞脉络丛脑膜炎病毒 (LCMV) 是一种啮齿类动物传播的乳腺病毒,虽然具有趋神经性和潜在的严重临床疾病,但在世界范围内流行且未被充分认识。LCMV 通常由家鼠(Mus musculus)携带,因此分布于全球城市和农村地区。传播 主要通过吸入受感染啮齿动物的雾化排泄物或受污染的分泌物发生,其他途径包括实体器官移植(很少)和垂直 传播。在人类中,LCMV 感染可能是一种不明显或自限性发热性疾病,也可能是更严重的疾病,如无菌性脑膜炎或脑膜脑炎,尤其是在免疫功能低下的患者中。据报道,先天性感染可导致脉络膜视网膜炎、颅内钙化、各种神经畸形、智力障碍、神经发育问题和胎儿死亡。迄今为止,文献中已记录了 88 例先天性 LCMV 感染病例,全球报告了 5 个供体来源的移植相关集群,涉及 17 名受者。本叙述性综述的目的是提供 LCMV 的全面且最新的概述。具体来说,该综述总结了目前对其病毒学特征、流行病学、发病机制、临床表现、诊断、治疗 和预防的认识。特别关注先天性感染、移植相关疾病和 LCMV 不断发展的 流行病学,重点关注其在“同一个健康”框架内的公共卫生相关性。还讨论了实验室方法和诊断挑战,包括相关的生物安全考虑因素。最后,审查强调了持续存在的知识差距,并确定了未来研究、监测 和公共卫生行动的优先领域。

papers.full_text: Abstract Mammarenaviruses are zoonotic pathogens that establish persistent infections in rodents and periodically spill over into humans, causing severe disease. Several species, including Lassa virus (LASV) and Junín virus (JUNV) are etiological agents of viral hemorrhagic fever (HF) disease associated with high morbidity and mortality rates. Given the absence of licensed vaccines or effective therapeutics, the development of broad-spectrum antivirals against mammarenaviruses remains an urgent biomedical priority. The mammarenavirus L protein encodes the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) and a highly conserved endonuclease (EndoN) domain that plays a critical role in cap-snatching mediated transcription of viral mRNA, making it an attractive antiviral target. Baloxavir acid (BXA), designed to inhibit the EndoN activity of the PA subunit of the influenza polymerase, also inhibited LCMV, JUNV, and LASV multiplication, albeit with limited potency. Guided by this finding, we conducted a medicinal chemistry campaign to modify the chemical scaffold of BXA and identified mCPB916 as a lead compound with broad-spectrum activity against multiple mammarenaviruses. Genetic, structural, and biochemical analyses confirmed mCPB916 targets the EndoN domain of the mammarenavirus L protein. Prophylactic treatment with mCPB916 significantly inhibited viral infection, reduced disease-associated pathology, and improved survival in mouse models of lethal LCMV and LASV infection. Together, these results define the structural basis and in vivo efficacy of mammarenavirus-specific EndoN inhibitors and establishes mCPB916 as a prototype EndoN inhibitor for the development of broad-spectrum antivirals against human pathogenic mammarenaviruses. papers.title_zh: 结构引导开发病毒核酸内切酶抑制剂,可有效限制体内人类致病性乳腺病毒感染
papers.source_body_en: Guided by this finding, we conducted a medicinal chemistry campaign to modify the chemical scaffold of BXA and identified mCPB916 as a lead compound with broad-spectrum activity against multiple mammarenaviruses. Together, these results define the structural basis and in vivo efficacy of mammarenavirus-specific EndoN inhibitors and establishes mCPB916 as a prototype EndoN inhibitor for the development of broad-spectrum antivirals against human pathogenic mammarenaviruses. Abstract Mammarenaviruses are zoonotic pathogens that establish persistent infections in rodents and periodically spill over into humans, causing severe disease. Several species, including Lassa virus (LASV) and Junín virus (JUNV) are etiological agents of viral hemorrhagic fever (HF) disease associated with high morbidity and mortality rates. Given the absence of licensed vaccines or effective therapeutics, the development of broad-spectrum antivirals against mammarenaviruses remains an urgent biomedical priority. The mammarenavirus L protein encodes the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) and a highly conserved endonuclease (EndoN) domain that plays a critical role in cap-snatching mediated transcription of viral mRNA, making it an attractive antiviral target. Baloxavir acid (BXA), designed to inhibit the EndoN activity of the PA subunit of the influenza polymerase, also inhibited LCMV, JUNV, and LASV multiplication, albeit with limited potency. Genetic, structural, and biochemical analyses confirmed mCPB916 targets the EndoN domain of the mammarenavirus L protein. Prophylactic treatment with mCPB916 significantly inhibited viral infection, reduced disease-associated pathology, and improved survival in mouse models of lethal LCMV and LASV infection. papers.title: Performance Evaluation of Machine Learning Models for Lassa Fever Prediction
papers.abstract: Lassa fever is a severe viral hemorrhagic illness endemic in parts of West Africa, primarily transmitted through contact with infected rodent excreta. Early detection and accurate diagnosis are critical to reducing mortality and controlling outbreaks. In recent years, machine learning (ML) has shown great potential in enhancing disease prediction and diagnostic accuracy. This study evaluates the performance of various ML models, including Logistic Regression, K-Nearest Neighbors, Support Vector Machine, and Naïve Bayes, in predicting Lassa fever infection. The models were trained and tested on a dataset comprising clinical and demographic features of patients. Key evaluation metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall (sensitivity), F1-score, macroaverage, and weighted-average were employed to assess model performance. The Support Vector Machine (SVM) model outperformed others with an accuracy of 90%, precision of 91%, recall of 96%, and an F1-score of 93%. The findings underscore the effectiveness of SVM in developing a diagnostic model for Lassa fever, providing a foundation for deploying AI-driven diagnostic tools in resource-limited settings. Future research should explore integrating more diverse datasets and incorporating additional clinical parameters to enhance prediction accuracy further.
papers.journal: WORLD JOURNAL OF INNOVATION AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY

papers.title: Lassa Fever Predictive Model Using Machine Learning Techniques
papers.abstract: Lassa Fever, a severe hemorrhagic fever caused by the Lassa virus, is notably prevalent in West Africa and can be fatal if not managed properly. Effective outbreak control and mitigation rely heavily on early detection. This study introduces a predictive model for forecasting Lassa Fever using machine learning techniques. The research employs an extensive dataset that includes epidemiological and environmental data collected over multiple years to construct a reliable predictive model. Several machine learning algorithms, such as Random Forest, Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Gradient Boosting, are utilized to analyze historical data and predict potential Lassa Fever outbreaks. To improve model accuracy and minimize false positives, feature engineering and data preprocessing methods are applied. The dataset was divided into 80% for training and 20% for testing, with various algorithms—including SVM, K-Nearest Neighbor, Naïve Bayes, and Logistic Regression—tested to build the predictive models. The performance of these models was assessed using metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. The SVM model demonstrated the highest performance, achieving accuracy, precision, and F1 scores of 90%, 91%, and 96%, respectively. Consequently, SVM was selected as the preferred algorithm for this research. The study recommends the use of this model in Nigeria's medical industry to enhance diagnostic speed and reduce medical errors in healthcare settings. Keywords: Lassa Fever, Predictive Model, Machine Learning, Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Healthcare Diagnostics
papers.journal: International Journal of Computer Science and Mathematical Theory

papers.title: Lassa Fever Burden and Reported Case Fatality in Nigeria from 2024 To Epidemiological Week 31 Of 2026: The Public Health Lessons
papers.abstract: Background: Lassa fever remains an important public health challenge in Nigeria. We assessed changes in reported disease burden, geographical distribution and case fatality between 2024 and epidemiological week 31 of 2026. Methods: We conducted a retrospective descriptive analysis of aggregate national surveillance data from Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention Lassa fever situation reports. Indicators included suspected and confirmed cases, deaths among confirmed cases, the confirmed to-suspected case proportion, and affected states and local government areas. Case-fatality ratios (CFRs) were calculated with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Exploratory two-sided pooled two-proportion z-tests compared CFRs. Epidemiological weeks 1–31 of 2025 and 2026 were compared to reduce bias from unequal observation periods. Results: Confirmed cases decreased by 12.3%, from 1,309 in 2024 to 1,148 in 2025, whereas deaths remained similar at 214 and 215. CFR increased from 16.35% (95% CI 14.44–18.45%) to 18.73% (16.58–21.09%; p = 0.121). By week 31 of 2026, 1,017 confirmed cases and 239 deaths were reported, yielding a CFR of 23.50% (21.00–26.20%). Compared with weeks 1–31 of 2025, confirmed cases increased by 21.7% and deaths by 53.2%; CFR increased from 18.66% to 23.50% (p = 0.011). The 2026 report attributed approximately 86% of confirmed cases to Ondo, Bauchi, Taraba, Edo and Benue. Conclusion: Reported Lassa fever fatality increased in early 2026, including in a comparison of equivalent surveillance periods. These findings support strengthening timely diagnosis, referral, supportive care and outcome surveillance, particularly in high-burden states. Aggregate data cannot establish the causes of the increase.
papers.journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF MEDICAL EVALUATION AND PHYSICAL REPORT

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:拉沙热 仍然是尼日利亚的一个重要公共卫生挑战。我们评估了 2024 年至 2026 年流行病学第 31 周期间报告的疾病负担、地理分布和病死率的变化。方法:我们对尼日利亚疾病控制和预防中心 拉沙热 情况报告的国家 监测 汇总数据进行了回顾性描述性分析。指标包括疑似病例和确诊病例、确诊病例中的死亡人数、确诊病例与疑似病例的比例以及受影响的州和地方政府区域。病死率 (CFR) 使用 Wilson 95% 置信区间 (CI) 计算。探索性双边合并二比例 z 检验比较了 CFR。对 2025 年和 2026 年第 1-31 周的流行病学进行比较,以减少观察期不同造成的偏差。结果:确诊病例减少了 12.3%,从 2024 年的 1,309 例减少到 2025 年的 1,148 例,而死亡人数仍相似,为 214 例和 215 例。病死率从 16.35%(95% CI 14.44–18.45%)增加到 18.73%(16.58–21.09%;p = 0.121)。到 2026 年第 31 周,报告了 1,017 例确诊病例和 239 例死亡,病死率为 23.50% (21.00–26.20%)。与2025年第1-31周相比,确诊病例增加21.7%,死亡人数增加53.2%;CFR 从 18.66% 增加至 23.50% (p = 0.011)。2026 年的报告将约 86% 的确诊病例归因于翁多、包奇、塔拉巴、埃多和贝努埃。结论:报告的 拉沙热 死亡率在 2026 年初有所增加,包括与同等 监测 时期的比较。这些发现支持加强及时的 诊断、转诊、支持性护理和结果 监测,特别是在高负担州。汇总数据无法确定增加的原因。

papers.title: Insights from SARS-CoV-2 nanopore genomic surveillance in Edo State, Nigeria
papers.abstract: Abstract In response to the COVID-19 pandemic, local SARS-CoV-2 nanopore sequencing capacity was established at Irrua Specialist Teaching Hospital (ISTH), a Lassa fever reference centre based in Edo State, Nigeria. This was enabled through training of local staff in Nigeria and Guinea in both laboratory and bioinformatic SARS-CoV-2 sequencing protocols. Between March 2020 and December 2023, the laboratory at ISTH conducted 29,643 diagnostic tests for SARS-CoV-2, of which 4,575 (15.4%) were positive. Between April and December 2022, 410 SARS-CoV-2 positive samples were selected and retrospectively sequenced in 19 runs. From these, 213 near-complete (> 93%) viral genomes were generated and submitted to GISAID. Phylogenetic and phylogeographic analyses supported that Nigeria served simultaneously as a source and recipient of SARS-CoV-2 lineages, driving global spread of the AY.36 Delta variant and receiving Omicron sublineages (BA.1.1 and BQ.1) from North America and Europe. Here we show that a pre-existing long-term laboratory capacity development program for Lassa virus, a high-risk pathogen, facilitated the successful integration of novel workflows for a new emerging pathogen.

papers.title_zh: 来自尼日利亚埃多州 SARS-CoV-2 纳米孔 基因组监测 的见解
papers.source_body_en: Abstract In response to the COVID-19 pandemic, local SARS-CoV-2 nanopore sequencing capacity was established at Irrua Specialist Teaching Hospital (ISTH), a Lassa fever reference centre based in Edo State, Nigeria. This was enabled through training of local staff in Nigeria and Guinea in both laboratory and bioinformatic SARS-CoV-2 sequencing protocols. Between March 2020 and December 2023, the laboratory at ISTH conducted 29,643 diagnostic tests for SARS-CoV-2, of which 4,575 (15.4%) were positive. Between April and December 2022, 410 SARS-CoV-2 positive samples were selected and retrospectively sequenced in 19 runs. From these, 213 near-complete (> 93%) viral genomes were generated and submitted to GISAID. Phylogenetic and phylogeographic analyses supported that Nigeria served simultaneously as a source and recipient of SARS-CoV-2 lineages, driving global spread of the AY.36 Delta variant and receiving Omicron sublineages (BA.1.1 and BQ.1) from North America and Europe. Here we show that a pre-existing long-term laboratory capacity development program for Lassa virus, a high-risk pathogen, facilitated the successful integration of novel workflows for a new emerging pathogen.

papers.title: Persistent infection is associated with divergent evolution of T cell repertoires.
papers.abstract: In chronic infection, T cell clones recognizing the same epitope are variably expanded, with some clones evolving to become dominant, while others are lost. Clonal expansion and changes in the repertoire reflect both T cell receptor-intrinsic (TCR-intrinsic) and -extrinsic factors, yet the individuality of TCR repertoires makes it difficult to disentangle how TCR sequence shapes clonal behaviors. To address this, we exploited the observation that TCRs can be grouped into clusters based on sequence similarity. Using complementarity-determining region 3β (CDR3β) sequencing data derived from lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus-specific CD8+ T cells from mice infected early and late in the course of chronic infection, we identified CDR3β clusters ubiquitously shared by all mice. The pattern of CDR3β cluster abundance was highly similar between mice at the early time point in both self-limiting and persistent infection models. Over the course of chronic infection, the pattern of cluster abundance diverged between mice and dominant clones emerged that did not share sequence similarity between mice. This repertoire divergence was not observed in self-limiting infection, where the pattern of cluster abundance established early in infection was stable between mice beyond resolution of infection. In chronic infection, the repertoires of stem-like and exhausted antigen-specific T cells remained similar over time within individual mice, suggesting clonal selection acts on the stem-like pool. Our findings suggest that antigen-specific CD8+ T cell clones expanded early in infection have CDR3β motifs that are shared between mice, supporting a role for TCR structural properties in determining the repertoire structure. Divergent patterns of repertoire composition later in chronic infection suggest that these shared CDR3β motifs are less important in patterning the repertoire than during the initial response and there is greater complexity in factors that sculpt the repertoire over the course of persistent antigen exposure.

papers.title_zh: 持续感染与 T 细胞库的不同 进化 相关。
papers.source_body_en: In chronic infection, T cell clones recognizing the same epitope are variably expanded, with some clones evolving to become dominant, while others are lost. Clonal expansion and changes in the repertoire reflect both T cell receptor-intrinsic (TCR-intrinsic) and -extrinsic factors, yet the individuality of TCR repertoires makes it difficult to disentangle how TCR sequence shapes clonal behaviors. To address this, we exploited the observation that TCRs can be grouped into clusters based on sequence similarity. Using complementarity-determining region 3β (CDR3β) sequencing data derived from lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus-specific CD8+ T cells from mice infected early and late in the course of chronic infection, we identified CDR3β clusters ubiquitously shared by all mice. The pattern of CDR3β cluster abundance was highly similar between mice at the early time point in both self-limiting and persistent infection models. Over the course of chronic infection, the pattern of cluster abundance diverged between mice and dominant clones emerged that did not share sequence similarity between mice. This repertoire divergence was not observed in self-limiting infection, where the pattern of cluster abundance established early in infection was stable between mice beyond resolution of infection. In chronic infection, the repertoires of stem-like and exhausted antigen-specific T cells remained similar over time within individual mice, suggesting clonal selection acts on the stem-like pool. Our findings suggest that antigen-specific CD8+ T cell clones expanded early in infection have CDR3β motifs that are shared between mice, supporting a role for TCR structural properties in determining the repertoire structure. Divergent patterns of repertoire composition later in chronic infection suggest that these shared CDR3β motifs are less important in patterning the repertoire than during the initial response and there is greater complexity in factors that sculpt the repertoire over the course of persistent antigen exposure.

papers.title: Antiviral CD8+ T cells Engage a Neuroimmune Circuit to Drive Anorexia
papers.abstract: Abstract Infection-induced anorexia is a conserved sickness response that contributes to host defense and tolerance1-3. Although innate immune mediators are known to induce anorexia through neuro-immune communication 1,4, whether and how adaptive immunity engages neural circuits to regulate feeding remains poorly understood. Here, we identify a neuro-immune pathway linking antigen-specific antiviral CD8+ T-cell responses to brainstem control of feeding during lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) infection. Antigen-specific CD8+ T cells were required for late-phase anorexia and neuronal activation in the nucleus of the solitary tract (NTS), where Vglut2+ excitatory neurons mediated feeding suppression. Mechanistically, CD8+ T cell-intrinsic ST2-MyD88 signaling promoted cytotoxic effector function and peripheral sympathetic nerve injury, while vagal afferent signaling conveyed peripheral neural perturbations to the brainstem. Chemical sympathetic denervation was sufficient to trigger NTS activation and anorexia, whereas sympathetic denervation before infection or disruption of the CD8+ T-cell effector program attenuated these responses. Together, our findings reveal that IL-33-ST2-MyD88 signaling programs antiviral CD8+ T-cell effector function to engage a peripheral sympathetic-vagal-brainstem axis that suppresses feeding. This work uncovers a neuro-immune mechanism by which adaptive antiviral immunity extends beyond pathogen control to orchestrate infection-associated behavioral adaptation.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 感染引起的厌食症是一种保守的疾病反应,有助于 宿主 防御和耐受1-3。尽管已知先天免疫介质可通过神经免疫通讯诱发厌食症 1,4,但适应性免疫是否以及如何参与神经回路来调节进食仍知之甚少。在这里,我们确定了一条神经免疫途径,将抗原特异性 抗病毒药物 CD8+ T 细胞反应与 淋巴细胞脉络丛脑膜炎病毒 (LCMV) 感染期间的脑干进食控制联系起来。晚期厌食症和孤束核 (NTS) 中的神经元激活需要抗原特异性 CD8+ T 细胞,其中 Vglut2+ 兴奋性神经元介导摄食抑制。从机制上讲,CD8+ T 细胞固有的 ST2-MyD88 信号传导促进细胞毒性效应器功能和周围交感神经损伤,而迷走神经传入信号传导将周围神经扰动传递至脑干。化学交感神经去神经足以引发 NTS 激活和厌食,而感染前的交感神经去神经或 CD8+ T 细胞效应程序破坏则减弱了这些反应。总之,我们的研究结果表明,IL-33-ST2-MyD88 信号传导程序 抗病毒药物 CD8+ T 细胞效应器功能可参与抑制进食的外周交感神经-迷走神经-脑干轴。这项工作揭示了一种神经免疫机制,通过该机制,适应性 抗病毒药物 免疫扩展到病原体控制之外,以协调与感染相关的行为适应。

papers.title: TOX and PD-1 are required for the maintenance of CD4 T cell precursors during chronic infection.
papers.abstract: In contrast with the well-established mechanisms that maintain exhausted CD8 T cells, our knowledge about the differentiation and in particular the molecular control of CD4 T cells in chronic infections is limited. Using the lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) infection model, we identified that CXCR5+TCF-1+ CD4 T cells, found mainly in secondary lymphoid organs, serve as precursors for the CD4 population. These cells transition into terminally differentiated cells and combine T follicular helper (TFH) cell features (IL-21 expression) with T helper 1 (TH1) cell characteristics (CXCR6 expression and IFN-γ and TNF secretion). In the CXCR5+TCF-1+ population, CD62L+ cells exhibit the highest re-expansion potential in adoptive transfer settings. All subsets express TOX and PD-1, which ensure the maintenance of the CD4 T cell population. Absence of either factor reduces the number of CD62L+ precursors and impairs their further differentiation. Overall, we define a hierarchical framework for CD4 T cell maintenance in chronic infection and reveal common mechanisms that sustain both exhausted CD4 and CD8 T cell responses.

papers.title: Characterizing the Biological Roles of the Arenavirus Exoribonuclease (exoN) in a Tri-Segmented Pichinde Virus System
papers.abstract: Arenaviruses, such as Lassa virus (LASV) and Junin virus (JUNV), cause severe and often lethal hemorrhagic fevers, for which there are no FDA-approved vaccines or effective therapeutics. The viral nucleoprotein (NP) contains a 3′-5′ exoribonuclease (exoN) domain to suppress type I interferon (IFN-I) induction. However, the precise biological roles of the NP exoN during infection remain poorly characterized for highly pathogenic arenaviruses due to biosafety constraints and challenges in generating viable exoN mutants. Utilizing a recombinant tri-segmented Pichinde virus (PICV) vector (rP18tri) suitable for BSL-2 research, we generated two exoN-deficient GFP reporter viruses, (NPm1)-G and (NPm2)-G, by mutating key catalytic residues, and inserted JUNV NP as a transgene within the mutant backbones. All recombinant viruses replicated efficiently in IFN-deficient Vero cells. In IFN-competent A549 cells, all viruses except for the wild-type reporter virus rP18tri-G failed to undergo multicycle replication, consistent with their differential inhibition of IFN-I responses. In contrast to rP18tri-G, which effectively suppressed IFN-I induction throughout the infection time course, exoN-deficient viruses induced robust early IFN-I responses, whereas expressing JUNV NP as a transgene suppressed early IFN-I induction at 16 hpi but failed to sustain suppression at later time points. Further examination during the first round of viral replication in A549 cells demonstrated that the absence of exoN activity is associated with markedly reduced viral gene expression and decreased infectious particle production. Together, these data demonstrate an essential role for NP exoN in mediating IFN-I suppression and suggest its biological functions in viral gene expression and infectious particle production within IFN-competent cells, highlighting its potential as a broad-spectrum therapeutic target.

papers.abstract_zh: 沙粒病毒,如拉沙病毒 (LASV) 和胡宁病毒 (JUNV),会引起严重且往往致命的出血热,目前尚无 FDA 批准的 疫苗 或有效的治疗方法。病毒核蛋白 (NP) 含有 3'-5' 核糖核酸外切酶 (exoN) 结构域,可抑制 I 型干扰素 (IFN-I) 诱导。然而,由于生物安全限制和生成可行的 exoN 突变体的挑战,对于高致病性 沙粒病毒,NP exoN 在感染过程中的精确生物学作用仍然不清楚。利用适合 BSL-2 研究的重组三段 Pichinde 病毒 (PICV) 媒介 (rP18tri),我们通过突变关键催化残基生成了两种外显子缺陷型 GFP 报告病毒 (NPm1)-G 和 (NPm2)-G,并将 JUNV NP 作为转基因插入突变主链内。所有重组病毒都能在缺乏 IFN 的 Vero 细胞中有效复制。在具有 IFN 活性的 A549 细胞中,除野生型报告病毒 rP18tri-G 之外的所有病毒均未能进行多周期复制,这与它们对 IFN-I 反应的差异抑制一致。与在整个感染过程中有效抑制 IFN-I 诱导的 rP18tri-G 不同,exoN 缺陷型病毒诱导了强烈的早期 IFN-I 反应,而表达 JUNV NP 作为转基因抑制了 16 hpi 的早期 IFN-I 诱导,但在以后的时间点未能维持抑制。在 A549 细胞中第一轮病毒复制期间的进一步检查表明,exoN 活性的缺失与病毒基因表达显着减少和感染性颗粒产生减少有关。总之,这些数据证明了 NP exoN 在介导 IFN-I 抑制中的重要作用,并表明其在 IFN 感受态细胞内病毒基因表达和感染性颗粒产生中的生物学功能,突出了其作为广谱治疗靶点的潜力。

analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 与在整个感染过程中有效抑制 IFN-I 诱导的 rP18tri-G 不同,exoN 缺陷型病毒诱导了强烈的早期 IFN-I 反应,而表达 JUNV NP 作为转基因抑制了 16 hpi 的早期 IFN-I 诱导,但在以后的时间点未能维持抑制。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 在具有 IFN 活性的 A549 细胞中,除野生型报告病毒 rP18tri-G 之外的所有病毒均未能进行多周期复制,这与它们对 IFN-I 反应的差异抑制一致。

papers.full_text: Cold tumors are poorly recognized by host immunity. Tumor tagging strategies—neoantigen, xenogeneic, and viral antigen tagging—endow tumor cells with identifiable antigens via engineered probiotics, oncolytic viruses, and mRNA delivery. These tactics yield compelling preclinical and clinical results, emerging as a novel promising strategy for cancer immunotherapy. Cold tumors are poorly recognized by anti-tumor immunotherapyAnti-tumor immunotherapy has emerged as a transformative pillar of modern cancer care, encompassing immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs, see Glossary), chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy, oncolytic virotherapy, and other innovative platforms. Despite remarkable advances, immunotherapies remain severely limited by intrinsic resistance, especially in patients harboring immunologically “cold” tumors. Cold tumors are typified by scarce intratumoral CD8+ T-cell infiltration, low tumor mutational burden, impaired antigen presentation, and a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) (1). Together, these traits render tumor cells nearly “invisible” to host immunity and drive broad therapeutic resistance. Thus, novel strategies that overcome immune ignorance and reawake anti-tumor immunity are highly desirable. Emerging evidence has highlighted tumor tagging as a powerful approach that enhances tumor immunological visibility and profoundly remodels the TME, converts “cold” tumors into immunologically “hot” lesions, and elicits robust and durable anti-tumor immune responses. Here, we provide a concise, forward-looking overview of state-of-the-art tumor tagging strategies, discuss their translational implications, and highlight how these approaches are reshaping the therapeutic paradigm for immunologically cold solid tumors. The concept and biological rationale of tumor taggingTumor tagging can be defined as the intentional placement of antigenic signals into tumors to increase their recognizability by the immune system. To date, tumor tagging strategies directed against tumors have yielded compelling preclinical and clinical findings. Here, we highlight three major classes of strategies advanced in recent years: neoantigen tagging, xenogeneic antigen tagging, and viral antigen tagging. Of note, tumor tagging is not merely a discrete technology, but rather a unifying design principle that can be deployed through diverse delivery platforms, including engineered probiotics, engineered oncolytic viruses (OVs), and mRNA-based systems. In the sections below, we discuss these approaches in detail.Neoantigen taggingNeoantigens serve as pivotal tumor-specific targets for precise cancer recognition and eradication, with therapeutic strategies encompassing personalized neoantigens tailored to individual mutational landscapes and public/shared neoantigens targeting recurrent driver mutations (e.g., KRAS, VHL, PBRM1) that enable off-the-shelf vaccine development (Figure 1A) (2–4). Neoantigens are efficiently delivered via multiple platforms including synthetic long peptides, mRNA (5), DNA, viral vectors (6, 7), and engineered probiotic vectors; among these, engineered probiotics enable tumor-targeted colonization, in situ neoantigen synthesis and release, concurrent activation of antigen-presenting cells, and remodeling of the immunosuppressive TME, thereby markedly enhancing immunogenicity (8). Preclinically, probiotic-based neoantigen vaccines elicit robust neoantigen-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T cell responses, drove profound TME reprogramming (reduced Tregs, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, and inhibitory macrophages), and achieved potent control or complete regression of primary and metastatic solid tumors in CT26 colorectal cancer and B16F10 melanoma models (8). In clinical trials, a phase I study of personalized synthetic long-peptide neoantigen vaccines in patients with resected high-risk clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC; NCT02950766) demonstrated 100% immunogenicity with favorable safety (2). All patients mounted robust vaccine-specific T cell responses, dominated by polyfunctional CD4+ memory T cells, and 7 out of 9 patients developed T cell reactivity against autologous tumor cells (2). Notably, the vaccine effectively targeted canonical ccRCC driver mutations including VHL, PBRM1, BAP1, KDM5C, and PIK3CA, with driver neoantigens showing significantly higher immunogenicity than passenger mutations (2). Collectively, these findings validate the robust translational potential of neoantigen-based strategies in precision cancer immunotherapy. Although personalized neoantigen tagging achieves impressive immunogenicity in early-phase clinical trials, several practical barriers persist. First, “turn-around time and cost” for whole-exome sequencing, neoantigen prediction, peptide/mRNA synthesis restrict broad deployment for personalized formats. Second, accurate neoantigen prioritization remains difficult; many predicted neoantigens fail to elicit tangible T-cell responses. Shared public neoantigen platforms partially bypass patient-tailored workflows but are limited by the low frequency of target driver mutations across patient cohorts. For probiotic-delivered neoantigen systems, inter-patient gut microbiome variability alters tumor colonization efficiency of engineered bacteria, and pre-existing anti-bacterial immunity may dampen therapeutic performance. In addition, safety risks including off-target microbial expansion require rigorous monitoring for in-vivo application.Figure 1Tumor-tagging strategies making cold tumors visible to immunotherapy. Three core tumor-tagging paradigms for immunotherapy: (A) Neoantigen tagging. Tumor sequencing and mutation profiling enable the identification and prioritization of candidate neoantigens. Selected neoantigens delivered by long peptides, DNA, mRNA, engineered probiotics, or oncolytic viruses, thereby enabling direct antigen delivery and/or intratumoral neoantigen expression, promoting antigen presentation, activation of neoantigen-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, tumor cell lysis, and remodeling of the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. (B) Xenogeneic antigen tagging. Oncolytic virus-mediated delivery of α1,3GT induces de novo αGal expression on tumor cells, triggering recognition by pre-existing anti-αGal antibodies and downstream effector responses, including complement activation, membrane attack complex formation, vascular injury, and thrombosis, culminating in hyperacute rejection-like tumor destruction. (C) Viral antigen tagging. mRNA-LNPs or engineered oncolytic viruses deliver viral antigens into tumors and recall or amplify pre-existing virus-specific memory CD4+ and CD8+ T cell responses, resulting in clonal expansion, enhanced cellular immunity, and tumor cell killing, while also creating opportunities for synergy with immune checkpoint blockade. Together, these approaches reshape the tumor microenvironment and support more effective immune-mediated tumor control.Scientific illustration diagram divided into three labeled sections describing tumor neoantigen tagging (A), xenogeneic antigen tagging (B), and viral antigen tagging (C), each showing stepwise mechanisms of antigen introduction, immune activation, and resulting tumor cell lysis in cancer immunotherapy according to labeled symbols, cell types, and molecular pathways.Xenogeneic antigen taggingTagging tumors with xenogeneic antigens represents a transformative immunotherapeutic strategy that repurposes evolutionary immunity for precision cancer treatment (9). This approach exploits the α1,3-galactosyltransferase (α1,3GT)–αGal–anti-Gal axis—a pathway uniquely absent in humans but highly active in most mammals—to redirect preformed natural immunity against tumors. Humans carry anti-αGal IgM/IgG antibodies generated by gut microbial stimulation, while lacking functional α1,3GT and thus unable to synthesize αGal epitopes. This evolutionary gap enables engineered oncolytic Newcastle disease virus (NDV-GT) to selectively deliver porcine α1,3GT into tumor cells, forcing de novoαGal expression exclusively on malignant cells without modifying normal tissues. In infected tumor tissue, αGal decoration triggers a localized hyperacute rejection-like cascade: anti-αGal antibodies rapidly bind tumor vasculature and cell surfaces, activating complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC) and antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC), inducing platelet-activating factor (PAF) release, fibrinogen deposition, and selective intratumoral microthrombosis (Figure 1B) (9). This dual vascular occlusion and immune cytotoxicity rapidly starve tumors of blood supply while amplifying innate and adaptive anti-tumor immunity. Preclinically, NDV-GT achieved complete tumor regression in CRISPR-engineered primary hepatocellular carcinoma cynomolgus monkeys, with safety confirmed in non-human primates showing no organ damage, minimal neutralizing antibody induction, and preserved viral efficacy (9). In a phase 1 interventional trial (ChiCTR2000031980) of 20 heavily pretreated patients with refractory metastatic solid tumors (including liver, ovarian, cervical, lung, esophageal, rectal, breast cancer and melanoma), intravenous NDV-GT achieved a 90.00% disease control rate (DCR), with 1 case of CR, 6 cases of PR, 11 cases of SD, and 2 cases of PD. Durable responses exceeding 6–36 months were observed in several subjects (9). Treatment was well-tolerated with only mild adverse events and no grade ≥3 toxicities, cytokine release syndrome, or neurotoxicity. Mechanistically, NDV-GT suppressed the Akt-IKK-NF-κB pathway to promote tumor apoptosis, while enhancing CD4+/CD8+ T-cell infiltration, dendritic cell maturation, and IFN-γ/TNF-α secretion to reverse immunosuppression (9). This xenogeneic antigen-tagging platform provides a clinically validated, safe, and broadly applicable strategy to convert “cold” tumors “hot” and enable systemic oncolytic virotherapy for diverse advanced malignancies. This approach leverages pre-existing circulating anti-αGal antibodies and does not depend on neoantigen identification. Still, translational obstacles remain. First, inter-individual variation in endogenous anti-αGal antibody titers can shape treatment efficacy; patients with low anti-αGal levels may exhibit attenuated complement-dependent and ADCC-mediated tumor damage. Second, intrapatient tumor heterogeneity creates variable viral infection efficiency across distinct tumor lesions; poorly infected tumor foci escape αGal antigen decoration and thereby evade immune attack. Third, although current phase-1 data show mild safety profiles, widespread intratumoral microthrombosis raises theoretical risks for systemic coagulation complications when treating large tumor burdens, which requires careful dose-escalation and patient stratification in further clinical studies.Viral antigens taggingViral antigen tagging capitalizes on population-wide pre-existing immunity elicited by routine vaccinations or prior viral infections, which establishes abundant pools of stable, high-affinity memory CD8+ T cells capable of naturally infiltrating tumors (10–12). This strategy stands out as a uniquely scalable, cost-effective, and broadly applicable antigen-tagging approach that circumvents the requirement for personalized neoantigen identification, synthesis, and validation. Clinically, this approach can be implemented through two translatable modalities: intratumoral or intravenous administration of engineered OVs, and therapeutic mRNA vaccines encoding target viral antigens (Figure 1C). Preclinical investigations have robustly validated this concept across diverse vector platforms: the H-TVAC (Hepatitis B tumor vaccine antigen complex) system utilizes HBsAg (Hepatitis B virus surface antigen)-expressing oncolytic vaccinia virus to redirect hepatitis B vaccine-elicited memory T cells against solid tumors (12); vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) and single-cycle adenovirus vectors encoding SARS-CoV-2 Mem or Spike antigens direct high-affinity T cell immunity into established melanoma and colorectal tumors (13). Beyond activating memory CD8+ T cells, viral antigen tagging also mobilizes bystander T (TBYS) cells within the TME. Emerging evidence indicates that tumor-irrelevant TBYS cells are abundant in the TME. To harness such TBYS cells for tumor eradication, oncolytic viruses encoding TBYS epitopes have been engineered to redirect pre-existing TBYS cells toward tumor cells, thereby driving potent tumor suppression in multiple preclinical models (14). Accordingly, engineered OVs encoding lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) or SARS-CoV-2 epitopes selectively engage TBYS cells to drive potent tumor elimination (14, 15). These alterations foster robust synergy with chemotherapy and PD-1/PD-L1 immune checkpoint blockade, significantly prolonging survival in preclinical models of melanoma, colorectal cancer, and triple-negative breast cancer (15).Notably, this strategy demands no patient-specific customization, as most individuals harbor long-lived memory immunity to common viruses—including influenza, SARS-CoV-2, LCMV, and hepatitis B virus—arising from natural infection or universal vaccination (Figure 1C) (10–12). Together, harnessing pre-existing antiviral immune memory through OV- or mRNA-mediated viral antigen tagging creates a universal, off-the-shelf platform that retrains the immune system to target cancers, resolving long-standing obstacles in the clinical translation of personalized immunotherapy and oncolytic virotherapy. This off-the-shelf concept relies on pre-established antiviral memory T-cell pools within individual patients. The major limitation lies in “inter-patient heterogeneity of memory repertoires”: history of infection or vaccination determines the magnitude and quality of available virus-specific memory T-cells. Patients lacking corresponding antiviral memory cannot benefit from a given viral-antigen tagging modality. Moreover, pre-existing neutralizing antibodies against oncolytic viruses can reduce vector delivery to tumor sites. papers.source_body_en: These tactics yield compelling preclinical and clinical results, emerging as a novel promising strategy for cancer immunotherapy. To date, tumor tagging strategies directed against tumors have yielded compelling preclinical and clinical findings. In clinical trials, a phase I study of personalized synthetic long-peptide neoantigen vaccines in patients with resected high-risk clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC; NCT02950766) demonstrated 100% immunogenicity with favorable safety (2). Collectively, these findings validate the robust translational potential of neoantigen-based strategies in precision cancer immunotherapy. Cold tumors are poorly recognized by host immunity. Tumor tagging strategies—neoantigen, xenogeneic, and viral antigen tagging—endow tumor cells with identifiable antigens via engineered probiotics, oncolytic viruses, and mRNA delivery. Cold tumors are poorly recognized by anti-tumor immunotherapyAnti-tumor immunotherapy has emerged as a transformative pillar of modern cancer care, encompassing immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs, see Glossary), chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy, oncolytic virotherapy, and other innovative platforms. Despite remarkable advances, immunotherapies remain severely limited by intrinsic resistance, especially in patients harboring immunologically “cold” tumors. Cold tumors are typified by scarce intratumoral CD8+ T-cell infiltration, low tumor mutational burden, impaired antigen presentation, and a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) (1). Together, these traits render tumor cells nearly “invisible” to host immunity and drive broad therapeutic resistance. papers.title: BATF controls IFN I production via DC-SCRIPT in plasmacytoid dendritic cells
papers.abstract: The basic leucine zipper ATF-like transcription factor (BATF) plays a pivotal role in coordinating various aspects of lymphoid cell biology, yet essential functions in plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs) have not been reported. Here, we demonstrate that BATF deficiency leads to increased interferon (IFN) I production in Toll-like receptor 9 (TLR9)-activated pDCs, while BATF overexpression has an inhibitory effect. BATF-deficient mice exhibit elevated IFN-I serum levels early in lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) infection. Integrated transcriptomics and ChIP-seq approaches identified the transcriptional regulator DC-SCRIPT as a direct target of BATF that suppresses IFN-I promoter activity by interacting with interferon regulatory factor 7 (IRF7). Genome-wide association study (GWAS) analyses further implicate BATF in pDC-mediated human diseases. Our findings establish a novel negative feedback axis in IFN-I regulation in pDCs during antiviral immune responses orchestrated by BATF and DC-SCRIPT, with broader implications for pDC- and IFN-I-mediated autoimmunity.

news.title: Engineered Viral Endonuclease Inhibitor Restricts Lethal Mammarenavirus Infections in Mice
news.excerpt: Scientists have synthesized a targeted viral endonuclease inhibitor, mCPB916, that significantly suppresses viral replication and protects mice against lethal mammarenavirus infections.
news.rss_summary_html: Scientists have synthesized a targeted viral endonuclease inhibitor, mCPB916, that significantly suppresses viral replication and protects mice against lethal mammarenavirus infections.

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, November 14, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Engineered Viral Endonuclease Inhibitor Restricts Lethal Mammarenavirus Infections in Mice by November 12, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 Engineered Viral Endonuclease Inhibitor Restricts Lethal Mammarenavirus Infections in Mice Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Researchers have developed a prototype antiviral compound, designated mCPB916, that targets the viral endonuclease domain of the mammarenavirus large protein to inhibit infection in preclinical animal models. In lethal challenge studies evaluating lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus and Lassa virus in mice, prophylactic administration of the inhibitor significantly suppressed viral replication, alleviated disease-associated pathology, and increased overall survival rates. The investigation addresses a critical therapeutic void for zoonotic mammarenaviruses, which naturally maintain persistent reservoirs in rodent populations and periodically transmit to humans to trigger severe, often fatal viral hemorrhagic fevers. Mammarenaviruses represent persistent public health threats due to the severity of the illnesses they cause and the complete absence of licensed vaccines or targeted therapeutics. Several members of the genus, most notably Lassa virus and Junín virus, serve as the causative agents of severe viral hemorrhagic fever syndromes characterized by high clinical morbidity and mortality. Because rodents act as natural reservoirs, periodic spillover events occur, creating recurrent risks for human communities in endemic territories. Developing broad-spectrum antiviral strategies capable of countering diverse pathogenic species across the genus has therefore remained an essential priority in biomedical research. The researchers focused on the mammarenavirus L protein as a potential antiviral target. The L protein encodes the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase and a highly conserved endonuclease domain. This endonuclease performs a critical cap-snatching mechanism required for transcribing viral messenger RNA, making the domain an exceptionally attractive target for therapeutic disruption. The investigative team examined baloxavir acid, which was designed to inhibit the endonuclease activity of the PA subunit of the influenza polymerase. Baloxavir acid also inhibited the multiplication of lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus, Junín virus, and Lassa virus. However, baloxavir acid inhibited the multiplication of these mammarenaviruses with limited potency. Guided by the structural features of the endonuclease pocket and the initial activity profile of baloxavir acid, the investigators conducted a structure-guided medicinal chemistry campaign to modify the core chemical scaffold. Through iterative chemical optimization, the team synthesized and identified mCPB916 as a superior lead compound demonstrating broad-spectrum inhibitory potency across multiple pathogenic mammarenaviruses. Comprehensive genetic, structural, and biochemical evaluations confirmed that the mechanism of action of mCPB916 relies directly on engaging the endonuclease domain of the mammarenavirus large protein. Following in vitro verification, the investigators evaluated the therapeutic potential of the lead candidate in vivo using established lethal rodent challenge models. Mice infected with lethal doses of either lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus or Lassa virus received prophylactic treatment regimens with mCPB916. The administered compound demonstrated robust protective efficacy in both animal models, resulting in significant reductions in viral loads, attenuation of severe systemic pathology, and significantly enhanced survival outcomes compared to untreated cohorts. Collectively, the study establishes the structural basis and proof of concept for deploying viral endonuclease inhibitors as broad-spectrum countermeasures against high-consequence mammarenaviruses. These findings establish mCPB916 as a prototype endonuclease inhibitor for the development of broad-spectrum antivirals against human pathogenic mammarenaviruses. news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, November 14, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Rodent Virus Lymphocytic Choriomeningitis Poses Severe Congenital and Transplant Infection Risks by November 12, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Rodent Virus Lymphocytic Choriomeningitis Poses Severe Congenital and Transplant Infection Risks Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A comprehensive narrative review authored by Silvia Cammisa and colleagues from the National Institute for Infectious Diseases Lazzaro Spallanzani in Rome and the National Center for Public Health and Pharmacy in Budapest underscores the pervasive yet overlooked public health threat posed by lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus. Despite its historical role as a primary recognized cause of human aseptic meningitis, clinical detections have remained sparse in modern surveillance records, leading to diagnostic underestimation. The synthesis highlights how this mammarenavirus presents an expansive clinical spectrum, stretching from self-limiting febrile episodes to severe meningoencephalitis, serious congenital malformations, and fatal donor-derived infections among solid organ transplant recipients. At the molecular level, lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus is classified within the Arenaviridae family and genus Mammarenavirus, forming pleomorphic, enveloped virions measuring 110 to 130 nanometers in diameter with a characteristic sandy interior created by embedded host ribosomes. Its helical nucleocapsid encases an ambisense, single-stranded RNA genome partitioned into two segments designated short and large. The short segment encodes the nucleoprotein, which orchestrates viral transcription and replication, and the glycoprotein precursor cleaved into envelope subunits GP1 and GP2 plus a stable signal peptide. The large segment encodes the matrix zinc-binding protein and an RNA-dependent RNA polymerase. Cellular attachment is heavily governed by the interaction between GP1 and host alpha-dystroglycan, though binding affinities diverge widely across strains; high-affinity variants such as Clone 13, Traub, and WE54 demonstrate distinct tissue tropism and viral persistence in animal models, whereas low-affinity variants such as Armstrong, E350, and WE2.2 rely on alternative attachment factors, including heparan sulfate proteoglycans. The epidemiological maintenance of lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus relies fundamentally on the house mouse, Mus musculus, which sheds immense viral quantities across nasal secretions, saliva, milk, semen, urine, and feces when infected prenatally due to immune tolerance. Secondary rodent species, such as hamsters, rats, and guinea pigs, are also susceptible to infection, although their capacities to sustain prolonged maintenance cycles remain less established. Human transmission takes place through inhalation of aerosolized rodent excreta, handling of contaminated dust, food contamination, or direct animal bites, alongside vertical and donor-derived pathways. Lineages IV and V have been recorded in wild rodents within the Caucasus and Spain, while the divergent Dandenong virus was detected during an Australian transplant cluster. Current European epidemiological investigations reveal an extensive disparity between active viral circulation within reservoir communities and documented human clinical cases, a discrepancy largely driven by absent systematic surveillance, nonspecific symptom profiles, and the scarcity of routine diagnostic panels. Seroepidemiological research from Hungary exemplifies this gap: a retrospective analysis of seventy-four cerebrospinal fluid samples from individuals with central nervous system infections of unidentified origin identified confirmed infections in 2.7 percent of cases, while a subsequent national study spanning 2017 to 2023 documented twenty-three acquired cases and two serologically confirmed congenital infections. Similarly, a retrospective investigation in Piedmont, Italy, evaluating 371 serum samples from patients suspected of rodent-borne infections uncovered an IgG seroprevalence rate of 2.7 percent, demonstrating prior exposure despite absent clinical diagnoses. Seroepidemiologic studies have also recorded exposure in pregnant cohorts in Philadelphia, where IgG seropositivity reached 2.4 to 2.7 percent, alongside seropositivity reaching 13 percent in Austrian zoo workers, 36 percent in Croatian rodents, and 37.5 percent in Slovakian rodents. The mechanisms governing human neuropathogenesis remain incompletely understood and rely primarily on experimental observations gathered from adult mouse and neonatal rat models rather than direct human clinical investigations. Following initial peripheral transmission and systemic replication, the virus accesses the central nervous system, likely via endothelial infection and subsequent disruption of the blood-brain barrier. In adult rodent models, acute central nervous system disease is fundamentally driven by host immunopathology rather than direct cytolytic damage caused by viral replication. Specifically, virus-specific CD8+ T lymphocytes release potent chemokines that trigger massive infiltrations of inflammatory monocytes and neutrophils into meningeal tissues, precipitating vascular leakage and severe intracranial pathology. In neonatal rat paradigms, experimental findings reveal that viral strain characteristics dictate distinct cellular affinities; strain E350 preferentially infects glial structures, whereas WE2.2 and Clone 13 preferentially target neuronal populations. Clinically apparent infections in immunocompetent hosts typically follow a mild or moderate course, though a notable portion of patients experience a characteristic biphasic trajectory marked by initial systemic illness followed by a neurological phase after a temporary symptom-free window. When aseptic meningitis develops, lumbar puncture reveals marked lymphocytic pleocytosis, with white cell counts extending from one hundred to several thousand cells per microliter and lymphocytes constituting greater than 80 percent of the cellular population. Mild to moderate hypoglycorrhachia is frequently documented, occasionally declining to fifteen milligrams per deciliter, or 0.83 millimoles per liter. A smaller subset of patients progresses to meningoencephalitis characterized by altered mental status, seizures, or focal deficits, typically presenting with normal neuroimaging or nonspecific inflammatory patterns. In sharp contrast to the self-limiting course seen in immunocompetent individuals, donor-derived transmission in solid organ transplantation results in catastrophic clinical disease marked by rapid progression, multi-organ failure, and exceptionally high mortality. Worldwide surveillance has documented five distinct transplant clusters encompassing seventeen organ recipients who received kidneys, livers, or lungs from donors harboring unrecognized, transient viral infections. In the United States clusters recognized in 2003 and 2005, eight organ recipients contracted the pathogen, resulting in seven fatalities within nine to seventy-six days post-transplantation; epidemiological tracing in the 2005 event linked the donor to an infected domestic pet hamster carrying an identical lineage I strain. Subsequent transplant transmissions in Massachusetts in 2008 and nationally in 2011 caused four additional patient deaths. In Australia, the novel Dandenong lineage caused the deaths of three female organ recipients within four to six weeks following transplantation from an infected donor. Congenital transmission represents another devastating clinical manifestation of lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus, with eighty-eight confirmed fetal cases recorded in published medical literature since the first description in England in 1955. Maternal exposure during pregnancy, which frequently manifests as a transient or asymptomatic febrile episode, permits transplacental viral dissemination into the developing fetal central nervous system, particularly during early gestational trimesters. A comprehensive clinical review by Pencole and colleagues evaluating sixty-eight congenital cases demonstrated that manifestations are dominated by chorioretinitis in 84 percent of cases, hydrocephalus in 53 percent, microcephaly in 31 percent, ventriculomegaly in 16 percent, and periventricular calcifications in 16 percent. Extracerebral complications include fetal growth restriction, hydrops fetalis, cardiomegaly, ascites, and anemia. Case records, such as an infection following a mouse bite at six weeks of gestation leading to extensive bilateral ventriculomegaly and termination at twenty-two weeks, underscore the critical necessity of including the virus within differential diagnoses for unexplained TORCH-negative congenital neuropathies. Establishing a reliable diagnosis demands a strategic multimodal approach tailored to the infection stage, as clinical signs overlap substantially with other infectious entities and commercially approved tests remain exceedingly rare. Molecular diagnosis using reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction serves as the primary method during early acute viremia and neuroinvasive phases, targeting conserved sequences within the nucleoprotein, large protein, or short genomic segment. A recently validated quantitative assay targeting the short segment demonstrated an analytical limit of detection of 5.6 genome copies per microliter across all five viral lineages. Serological evaluation utilizing enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays and indirect immunofluorescence assays evaluates IgM and IgG antibodies, though single IgM determinations remain merely presumptive and require confirmation via paired sera demonstrating significant titer elevations. Diagnosticians must also navigate cross-reactivity with related mammarenaviruses and recognize that antibody responses are frequently absent in immunosuppressed transplant recipients. Culturing replication-competent virus in BHK-21, L-929, or Vero cells remains limited to research facilities due to weak cytopathic effects and specialized BSL-3 or ABSL-3 containment requirements. Therapeutic options for human infection remain strictly supportive, as no antiviral agents or protective human vaccines have demonstrated definitive efficacy in controlled clinical trials. For uncomplicated meningitis cases, clinical management focuses on analgesia, hydration, and monitoring, while transplantation-associated disease requires urgent reduction of pharmacological immunosuppression accompanied by individualized salvage regimens involving the broad-spectrum guanosine analogue ribavirin. Preclinical evaluations have identified several direct-acting antiviral candidates, including the nucleoside analogues favipiravir, 4′-fluorouridine, and its orally available prodrug VV251, along with cap-dependent endonuclease inhibitors and monoclonal neutralizing antibodies targeting viral surface glycoproteins. Because therapeutic measures remain restricted, public health strategies emphasize primary prevention through comprehensive rodent control programs, safe disposal of household infestations using wet cleaning techniques to suppress airborne aerosols, and the utilization of personal protective equipment. Furthermore, enhanced One Health epidemiological surveillance and rigorous donor exposure questionnaires are imperative to mitigate transmission risks across vulnerable obstetric and organ transplant populations worldwide.
